cards.name: Tab 2 - White
cards.summary: Symbol 'Tab 2 - White' from Illustrator's Web Buttons and Bars symbol library: a smooth-gradient tab: a rectangle with rounded top corners and a square bottom edge in near-white shading to very light grey, with a faint pale-grey outline along the top edge; the artwork is white and is shown on the renderer's mid-grey backing. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 132 x 38 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: the active tab joined to a white content panel in web mock-ups
avoid: a labelled tab: it is blank; add the text with the Type tool
a closed button: the tab has square bottom corners so it can sit on a panel; use a Button symbol for a free-standing control
a white or light background where the tab itself must stand out: the artwork is near-white (raw export: about 227-249) and nearly vanishes; place it on a blue, grey or dark ground
a flat or modern look: the gloss, gradient and highlight are baked in; break the link and set flat fills for a flat UI
cards.applies_to: the artboard of an open document: placing it creates a symbol instance, a linked copy of the symbol definition that can be moved, scaled and rotated like any object; the symbol must exist in the target document (placing from the library copies it in)
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Symbol Libraries > Web Buttons and Bars; click the symbol (it is added to the Symbols panel), then drag it onto the artboard or press Place Symbol Instance. Script: doc.symbolItems.add(doc.symbols.getByName("Tab 2 - White")) in a document that holds the symbol; to use it in another document: app.open("<Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Symbols/Web Buttons and Bars.ai"), place an instance there, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the symbol arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: On the mid-grey backing: rounded-top tab in a smooth near-white (248) to very light grey (227) gradient with a faint pale-grey top outline.

review.changes: avoid: white confirmed from the raw export, hedge removed and the line narrowed so it no longer contradicts use_for (joined to a white panel); confidence medium -> high
